check_notes.A1-2: No proposer-maintenance rule in the OpenZeppelin Governor used by ENS: nothing cancels a proposal if the proposer falls below 100,000 ENS delegated during voting (EP 5.15 discusses only the voting delay, not proposer maintenance).
check_notes.A1-3: No live autonomous/bond proposal path. EP 5.15 (social, passed) approves a 1,000 ENS ProposalBond design in principle; it is not implemented, so the 100,000 ENS threshold remains the only gate.
check_notes.A1-4: No explicit max actions per proposal stated in ENS docs. Payloads are bounded in practice only by block gas limits; no stated max verified.
check_notes.A2-1: Voting delay is 1 block (EP 5.15: 'the voting delay period which is currently set to only one block'). EP 5.15 proposes a 24-hour delay; not yet in force at snapshot date.
check_notes.A2-4: No vote-differential rule: executable proposals pass on a simple majority plus the 1% quorum. The two-thirds rule for constitutional amendments is an approval threshold, not a differential.
check_notes.A2-6: Delegated share measured: 3,980,000 ENS of 100,000,000 (3.98%) delegated (Tally, 2026-11-10). Per-delegate / top-holder concentration (HHI) not measured: Tally delegate voting powers were not captured in the snapshot — disclosed as a limitation.
check_notes.A3-2: No grace period stated in ENS docs for the OpenZeppelin TimelockController; whether queued operations expire was not verified from a primary source at audit time.
check_notes.A3-5: Upgrade path is via passed executable proposals through the governor/timelock (docs: executable proposals can upgrade an ENS core contract), but the controlling authority for the ENS root and the pending Governor Nexus changes were not verified as a single documented path.
check_notes.A4-1: Treasury moves mostly via timelocked governance, but the Treasury Flow Automation proposal grants Karpatkey a scoped permission to send ETH/USDC to wallet.ensdao.eth without a proposal; the timelock keeps a 6-month USDC runway (~$8M).
check_notes.A4-3: Standing bound exists in part: the Treasury Flow Automation policy keeps a 6-month runway (~$8M USDC) in the timelock. No per-operation whitelist or cap schedule was verified.
check_notes.A5-3: New council members are named individuals (EP 6.50) and the 5-of-8 threshold is published, but the official docs page still describes the expired 4-of-8 council, so the published composition is inconsistent across primary sources.
check_notes.A5-4: New council term runs to 2028-07-16 with an expiry mechanism carried from the 2024 design, but the docs page still describes the old council whose authority expired 2026-07-24; the renewal path was demonstrated (EP 6.45 defeated, EP 6.50 re-founded) rather than documented as a rule.
check_notes.A6-1: Voting delay (1 block) is stated only in EP 5.15, not in the main governance-process doc; the timelock grace period is not stated anywhere in ENS docs.
check_notes.A6-4: Direct discrepancy: docs.ens.domains/dao/security-council states a 4-of-8 council, while EP 6.50 (July 2026) seated a 5-of-8 council for a term to 2028-07-16.
